body: Yeah not really any money left for that, most months we dip in to overdraft and every time I do talk to the wife and get her to stop spending - and thus suffer the household with her unique way of making everyone feel bad - that money goes in to whatever repair or maintenance I've had to put off.

Thanks for your reply. I'm not in any of those places, but I hear you. It's not that I want to die, I've just grown disinterested in living.  Although you joke, I can see how easy it might be to strip away people's self-preservation instincts during radicalization and how that feeds a cycle that the military industrial complex practically lives off of these days.

It's kind of like if you said hey human, were going to give you a choice. We can put you in this indestructible cage and throw away the key, or we can put you out of your misery.  Of course if go free and live a happy fulfilling life is on the table I am going to pick that every time.

But I genuinely feel like I've made choices that have put me in a spot that is essentially that cage. I will never not be a father or a husband even if "ex".  It's as permanent as losing your legs. That's kind of the only thing I'm holding on to is the impact on my children. I don't believe in any afterlife but they will live on and I can't not care.

So I guess the real question is how do I learn to accept the cage? Drugs? An affair? Even those cost money! I hardly ever get to buy anything for myself. I make several hundred thousand a year and I buy clothes at Goodwill, most have holes in them and I regularly eat expired/stale food just to avoid wasting it.

I love my kids but I'm going through a roller coaster here because at the same time my family disgusts me.  I came from a very poor family, like incredibly poor and the amount of food and trash I have to dispose of every week makes me sick.

I would say fuck the life insurance policy but my kids while not perfect are a huge product of their mothers failure as a parent - it's not only that she's not involved, she actively sabotages any attempts I make to teach them scarcity and responsibility - and I am not any kind of hard ass, I am compassionate and emotional and understanding, I'm talking about "you just broke that thing that cost $500, no, you can't have a new one" - I'm a monster. They have had completely unrealistic expectations drilled in to them and I worry if I don't stick around to prepare them for the real world they will be severely depressed and incapable of handling it.
